q: What happens if the share drops in the middle of saving my project?
a: Nothing is lost. For a project on a network share, File ▸ Save (`file.save`) first writes the same project to `<data folder>/network-backups/<name>-<number>.fcproj` on this computer, then writes to the share. If the share stops answering (or the disk is full, or the file reads back different), the save reports an error ending with This save is kept on this computer: and the local copy's path. Open that file with File ▸ Open (`file.open`) to carry on, and save it back to the share once it works again.

q: Why does saving to a network share need extra care?
a: Every Revolution save writes to a temporary file next to the project, flushes it to disk and swaps it in, so a crash mid-save never leaves half a file. Over SMB that swap isn't always as safe as on a local disk, so for a project on a share Revolution also keeps a local copy first, reads the saved file back to compare, and keeps auto-saves on this computer.

q: How many versions does the network-backups folder keep?
a: Only the latest save per project. The file is `<data folder>/network-backups/<name>-<number>.fcproj`; the number tells apart projects with the same name in different places. For older versions, look at the auto-saves.

q: Can I keep auto-saves next to a project that lives on the NAS?
a: By default no: for a project on a share, auto-save versions go to the data folder's Auto-Save folder on this computer instead of an Auto-Save folder next to the project. If you choose a folder yourself in Project Settings ▸ Scratch Disks ▸ Project Auto Save, Revolution uses that folder.

q: Does saving a project on my local disk also make a network backup?
a: No. The local copy, the read-back and the local auto-saves apply only when the project file is on a network share. For a project on a local disk the save's result has `localCopy: null`; the usual temporary-file-and-swap save still protects it.

q: Why can't a crash mid-save leave me with half a project file?
a: Every save writes the project to a temporary file next to it, flushes that to disk and only then swaps it in place of the old file, so the old file stays whole until the new one is complete. On a network share Revolution adds a local copy first and a read-back check, because the swap isn't always as safe over SMB.

q: The save error gave me a path ending in .fcproj under network-backups. What is that?
a: That is the local copy Revolution wrote before saving to the share; the save to the share failed, so this is your latest work. Open it with File ▸ Open (`file.open`) and carry on editing; when the share works again, save it back there (File ▸ Save As, `file.saveAs`).

q: Does it check the file afterwards too?
a: Yes. After the save, Revolution reads the file on the share back and compares it with what it saved; if it differs, the save reports an error ending with This save is kept on this computer: and the local copy's path, so you can carry on from that copy.
prev: Does Revolution do anything special when the project file is on a server?

q: and the autosaves, do they end up on the server too?
a: No: for a project on a network share, auto-save versions go to the data folder's Auto-Save folder on this computer, not next to the project on the share, unless you chose a folder in Project Settings ▸ Scratch Disks ▸ Project Auto Save.

context.q: my project file lives on our office server, is saving ok?
context.a: Yes: for a project on a share, every save first writes a copy to network-backups in the data folder on this computer, then saves to the share and reads it back to compare; if that fails, the error names the local copy to open.
